question.problem: The duration of a tv program is uniformly distributed between $52$ and $66$ minutes, inclusive. What is the probability that a randomly chosen program lasts $60$ minutes or less?
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the duration of the tv program. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U[52,66],$ and we wish to compute $P(X\le 60).$

In general, if $X∼U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a}, & a\le x\le b \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

So, for our random variable $X∼U[52,66],$ we have the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{14}, & 52\le x\le 66 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 60) & ={\int }_{52}^{60}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{52}^{60}\frac{1}{14}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{x}{14}|}_{52}^{60} \\  & =\frac{60}{14}-\frac{52}{14} \\  & =\frac{4}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
